s:
Match List–I with List–II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.
List–I (Authors) List–II (Works)

a. Pavuluri Mallana
I. Kreedabhiramam

b. Vinukonda Vallabharaya
II. Ganitasara Sangraham

c. Aryadeva
III. Chittasuddhi Prakarana

d. Dignaga
IV. Pramana Samucchaya
x:
Pavuluri Mallana translated Ganitasara Sangraham, an important mathematical treatise originally composed by Mahaviracharya. His work helped introduce advanced mathematical concepts into Telugu literary tradition. Vinukonda Vallabharaya authored Kreedabhiramam, a celebrated Telugu literary work depicting social life and courtly culture during the Vijayanagara period. Aryadeva, one of the foremost disciples of Nagarjuna, composed Chittasuddhi Prakarana, an important Buddhist philosophical treatise dealing with the purification of mind and Madhyamika philosophy. Dignaga, regarded as the founder of the Buddhist school of logic, authored Pramana Samucchaya, a foundational work on Buddhist epistemology and logic that greatly influenced later Indian philosophy. Thus, the correct matching is a–II, b–I, c–III, d– IV, corresponding to Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Pavuluri Mallana – Ganitasara Sangraham
• Vinukonda Vallabharaya – Kreedabhiramam
• Aryadeva – Disciple of Nagarjuna
• Dignaga – Father of Buddhist Logic

s: Who is said to have written 'Andhrashabda Chintamani'?
x:
Nannaya Bhattu, popularly known as the Adi Kavi of Telugu, is traditionally credited with writing Andhra Shabda Chintamani, the earliest known grammatical treatise on the Telugu language. Although the original work is no longer available, later grammarians frequently referred to it, establishing Nannaya's reputation as the first Telugu grammarian. Apart from grammar, he also began the Telugu translation of the Mahabharata under the patronage of Rajaraja Narendra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Author – Nannaya Bhattu
• Work – Andhra Shabda Chintamani

s: Who received the Agrahara of Navakhandavada from Rajaraja Narendra?

Pavuluri Mallana, the famous mathematician and author of the Telugu Ganitasara Sangraham, received the Navakhandavada Agrahara from Rajaraja Narendra. He is regarded as one of the earliest mathematicians to compose scientific literature in Telugu. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Navakhandavada Agrahara → Pavuluri Mallana

Who composed Basava Puranam?
x:
Palkuriki Somanatha was one of the greatest Shaivite poets of the Kakatiya period. He composed the famous Basava Puranam, which narrates the life and teachings of Basaveswara, the founder of the Veerashaiva (Lingayat) movement. Written in simple Telugu Dwipada metre, the work made religious literature accessible to common people. It emphasizes equality, devotion to Shiva, dignity of labour and opposition to caste discrimination. Apart from Basava Puranam, Palkuriki Somanatha also authored Panditaradhya Charitra and several other important Shaivite works. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Author – Palkuriki Somanatha
• Work – Basava Puranam
• Literary Form – Dwipada

s: Who translated Mahaviracharya's 'Ganitasarasangraham' into Telugu?
x:
Pavuluri Mallana translated Mahaviracharya's Ganitasara Sangraha into Telugu, making one of India's earliest mathematical treatises accessible to Teluguspeaking scholars. Ganitasara Sangraha, originally composed in Sanskrit by Mahaviracharya during the 9th century, deals with arithmetic, algebra, geometry, fractions, mensuration and various mathematical problems. Mallana's Telugu version played an important role in popularizing mathematical knowledge in Andhra and is regarded as one of the earliest scientific works available in Telugu literature. This work demonstrates that medieval Telugu scholars contributed not only to literature but also to scientific and mathematical learning. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Original Author – Mahaviracharya

b. Marana

d. Manchena
IV. Keyurabahu Charitra
x:
Ketana was a disciple of Tikkana and authored Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, regarded as one of the earliest extant works on Telugu grammar. Marana translated the Markandeya Purana into Telugu under the patronage of the Kakatiyas, making it one of the earliest Telugu Puranas. Tikkana, one of the Kavitrayam, composed Nirvachanottara Ramayanam and translated fifteen parvas of the Mahabharata into Telugu. Manchena authored Keyurabahu Charitra, an important Telugu literary work based on courtly themes. Thus, the correct sequence is a–III, b–I, c–II, d– IV, corresponding to Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Ketana – Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam
• Marana – Markandeya Puranam
• Tikkana – Nirvachanottara Ramayanam
• Manchena – Keyurabahu Charitra
